stem: A client with diabetes is prescribed a beta-blocker and says tachycardia is a main warning sign used to recognize hypoglycemia. What should the nurse teach?

options.A: Expect beta-blocker therapy to make tachycardia a more reliable warning of hypoglycemia, so pulse changes can be trusted more strongly.
options.B: Teach that beta-blockers may mask some hypoglycemia warning signs, so glucose monitoring remains important when symptoms are less obvious.
options.C: Teach that beta-blockers eliminate the need for glucose monitoring because clinically important hypoglycemia becomes unlikely during treatment.
options.D: Expect beta-blockers to prevent hypoglycemia during exercise or missed meals, so routine glucose checks can safely be reduced.

rationale: HUMULIN R labeling states that antiadrenergic drugs such as beta-blockers can reduce or eliminate signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia. Glucose monitoring remains essential because warning symptoms may be less apparent. Therefore B is correct; A reverses the effect, and C/D falsely remove monitoring or claim prevention of hypoglycemia.
educational_objective: Teach clients that beta-blockers can blunt hypoglycemia warning symptoms and that glucose monitoring remains important.

source_original.stem: A client with diabetes is prescribed a beta-blocker and says tachycardia is a main warning sign used to recognize hypoglycemia. What should the nurse teach?

options.A: Expect beta-blocker therapy to make tachycardia a more reliable warning of hypoglycemia, so pulse changes can be trusted more strongly.
options.B: Teach that beta-blockers may mask some hypoglycemia warning signs, so glucose monitoring remains important when symptoms are less obvious.
options.C: Teach that beta-blockers eliminate the need for glucose monitoring because clinically important hypoglycemia becomes unlikely during treatment.
options.D: Expect beta-blockers to prevent hypoglycemia during exercise or missed meals, so routine glucose checks can safely be reduced.

source_original.rationale: Current insulin labeling notes that antiadrenergic drugs such as beta-blockers can reduce or eliminate some signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia. Option B is correct because it warns that symptom recognition may be blunted and reinforces glucose monitoring. Option A incorrectly makes tachycardia more reliable. Option C incorrectly removes monitoring. Option D incorrectly states that beta-blockers prevent hypoglycemia.
